script-basics.r: A script deleted files in the wrong folder because a variable was empty and the path became the root of the project. Quoting variables and checking for empty values would have turned a disaster into an error message.
script-basics.x: Shell is easy to start and easy to get wrong. Quote everything, validate inputs, fail early and keep scripts short. Once it needs real data structures or tests, move it to a better language.

control-flow-and-functions.r: A deployment script used a loop over a list of hosts but ignored failures, so it reported success when two hosts had not updated. Checking each exit code and summarising failures at the end showed the true state.
control-flow-and-functions.x: Exit codes are the contract between commands. Handle them explicitly, keep functions small with clear inputs and outputs, and make scripts safe to run twice.

text-processing.r: During an incident, a one-line pipeline with grep, awk, sort and uniq showed that one client address caused most of the errors. The answer came in a minute instead of waiting for a dashboard.
text-processing.x: Pipelines are fast tools for exploration, but fragile for production. Know the failure modes of parsing text meant for humans, and prefer structured output when the tool offers it.

advanced-patterns.r: A script parsed arguments by position, and when someone added an option the order broke silently. Switching to getopts made options explicit and gave useful error messages.
advanced-patterns.x: Interface design matters even in small scripts: stable options, helpful usage text and predictable exit codes. Avoid cleverness that the next person must decode at 3 a.m.

apis-and-json.r: A script that polled an API ignored pagination and only processed the first hundred results. Everything looked fine until the dataset grew. Following the next-page links and failing on unexpected responses fixed it.
apis-and-json.x: Calling APIs from shell needs timeouts, retries with backoff, rate limit awareness and care with secrets in process lists and logs. Parse JSON with jq, never with regular expressions.

safe-automation.r: A nightly script started again before the previous run had finished and the two corrupted a shared file. A lock file and strict mode with a cleanup trap prevented overlapping runs.
safe-automation.x: Automation must be safe to fail. Use strict mode with understanding of its gaps, locks against overlap, idempotent steps, timeouts and alerts when a scheduled job does not run at all.

arrays-and-parameter-expansion.r: A script split a list of file names on spaces and broke on a file called 'q3 report.csv'. Using an array and quoting each element handled names with spaces correctly.
arrays-and-parameter-expansion.x: Word splitting and globbing cause many bugs. Use arrays for lists, parameter expansion instead of external commands where it is simpler, and avoid parsing the output of ls.

building-and-testing-shell-tools.r: A helper script used by the whole team broke after a small change and nobody noticed for a week. Adding a few bats tests and running shellcheck in CI caught the next regression immediately.
building-and-testing-shell-tools.x: A script others depend on is a product. Version it, document it, test its failure paths and keep backward compatibility, or users will pin old copies and drift apart.

temporary-files-and-atomic-writes.r: A config file was rewritten in place, and a reader loaded it halfway through the write and crashed. Writing to a temporary file in the same directory and renaming it made the update atomic.
temporary-files-and-atomic-writes.x: Atomic rename, locks and unique temporary names remove whole classes of race conditions. Remember that rename is only atomic within one filesystem, and that locks need cleanup after a crash.

portable-scripts-and-shellcheck.r: A script that worked on a laptop failed on a minimal container because it used Bash features and the container only had a basic shell. Declaring the interpreter, avoiding bashisms where needed and running shellcheck found it before release.
portable-scripts-and-shellcheck.x: Decide the supported shells and tools up front and test on them. Lint on every change, and treat warnings as defects, since they usually point at real quoting or portability problems.

debugging-shell-scripts.r: A script worked on one run and did nothing on the next. Running it with tracing showed a command returned an unexpected empty result and the script carried on. Strict mode turned that silent failure into an immediate error.
debugging-shell-scripts.x: Make failure visible: tracing for investigation, strict mode for production, meaningful messages and logs. Reproduce with the same environment, since many shell bugs come from the environment, not the code.
